sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: DeerFlow is an open-source super agent harness from ByteDance. It coordinates sub-agents, memory and sandboxes so an AI agent can research, code, build slides or run data pipelines on its own, through a web UI at localhost.
sixtySeconds.problem: Building an agent that does long, multi-step work means wiring up planning, tools, file sandboxes, memory and a UI yourself. DeerFlow ships all of that ready to run, built on LangGraph and LangChain, and works with any OpenAI-compatible model.
whoFor: Developers wanting a ready-made deep research agent
Teams building autonomous agents on LangGraph
Self-hosters who want an agent with sandboxes and memory
Builders connecting agents to Slack, Telegram or GitHub
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a batteries-included agent runtime you can run locally and extend. It can execute commands, so run it only in a trusted environment.
requirements: Docker (recommended), or Node.js 22+, pnpm, uv and nginx
An API key for an OpenAI-compatible model

overview: DeerFlow started as a deep research framework. Version 2.0 is a ground-up rewrite into a general agent harness that shares no code with v1, which is kept on the 1.x branch. It orchestrates sub-agents, memory and sandboxes on top of LangGraph and LangChain.

It includes workspace file tools and isolated shells, skills and built-in tools, MCP servers, long-term memory, agentic browser control, scheduled tasks, private knowledge retrieval with RAGFlow, IM channels such as Slack, Telegram and Discord, GitHub event-driven agents, a terminal workbench and tracing through LangSmith or Langfuse.

Setup uses make: a wizard writes config.yaml and .env, then you start it with Docker or locally, and open localhost:2026. The README recommends models with long context, reasoning, multimodal input and strong tool use. It warns that DeerFlow can run commands and read and write files, so it is meant for a local trusted environment.

troubleshooting.solution: Run make doctor; it flags placeholder API keys. Replace them with real keys.
The local commands use the pnpm version pinned in frontend/package.json, through Corepack when available.

troubleshooting.problem: Want to run it on a server
troubleshooting.solution: Read the Security Notice first; an admin account is equivalent to code execution on the host.

troubleshooting.problem: Looking for the old Deep Research version
troubleshooting.solution: v1 is maintained on the 1.x branch.
